# Methods for Inhibiting Cell Proliferation and Treating GNAQ Mutation-Associated Diseases

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention relates to methods and compositions for inhibiting cell proliferation, treating vascular malformations, and identifying therapeutic agents relevant to diseases associated with specific mutations in the GNAQ gene.

## Method of Inhibiting Cell Proliferation

In one aspect, the invention provides a method of inhibiting cell proliferation and/or reducing the survival of cells that carry a GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutation. According to this method, cells harboring one of these mutations are contacted with puromycin or a puromycin analog. Exposure to the agent results in inhibition of proliferation, reduction in cell survival, or both, thereby selectively affecting cells that bear the mutant GNAQ genotype.

## Method of Treating Vascular Malformations

In a related aspect, the invention features a method of treating vascular malformations or related conditions in a subject. The method comprises administering to the subject an effective amount of puromycin or a puromycin analog. By delivering a therapeutically effective dose, the method addresses the underlying pathology associated with GNAQ mutations, providing a treatment approach for vascular malformations and conditions arising from or related to such mutations.

## Method of Identifying Candidate Therapeutic Agents

The invention further includes a method for identifying candidate agents capable of modulating diseases associated with a GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutation. This screening method enables the discovery of compounds with potential therapeutic utility in the context of GNAQ mutation-associated diseases.

In practicing this screening method, cells containing a mutant GNAQ gene are contacted with both puromycin and a candidate agent. Following exposure, the viability of the treated cells is assessed and compared to a reference level of cell viability. An alteration in cell viability relative to the reference level indicates that the candidate agent modulates the GNAQ mutation-associated disease. In this way, the method provides a reliable means of distinguishing agents that influence the disease phenotype from those that do not, thereby facilitating the identification of promising therapeutic candidates.

# Treatment of GNAQ Mutation-Associated Diseases Using Puromycin and Puromycin Analogs

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to methods and compositions for the treatment of diseases and conditions associated with mutations in the GNAQ gene, particularly the R183Q and Q209L mutations. More specifically, the invention provides therapeutic approaches utilizing puromycin and puromycin analogs to selectively target cells harboring these mutations, as well as screening platforms for identifying additional therapeutic agents.

## Background

The GNAQ gene encodes the Gαq subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, which plays a critical role in cellular signal transduction pathways. Certain somatic mutations in GNAQ, notably the R183Q and Q209L substitutions, result in constitutive activation of downstream signaling cascades. These activating mutations have been implicated in the pathogenesis of a range of disorders, including vascular malformations, which can cause significant morbidity and, in some cases, life-threatening complications.

Vascular malformations associated with GNAQ mutations often present therapeutic challenges, as conventional treatment modalities may be invasive, incompletely effective, or associated with substantial recurrence rates. Accordingly, there remains a significant unmet need for targeted therapeutic strategies that specifically address the underlying molecular drivers of these conditions.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention is directed to the discovery that puromycin and puromycin analogs exhibit a selective inhibitory effect on cells bearing GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutations. By contacting affected cells with these agents, the invention provides a means to inhibit cellular proliferation and reduce the survival of mutation-bearing cells, thereby offering a novel therapeutic avenue for the treatment of associated diseases.

## Detailed Description

### Therapeutic Methods

In one aspect, the invention provides methods for treating diseases and conditions associated with GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutations. These methods comprise contacting cells harboring the mutation with a therapeutically effective amount of puromycin or a puromycin analog. Upon contact, the agent acts to inhibit the proliferation of the affected cells and to reduce their overall viability and survival.

The methods disclosed herein are applicable to a variety of conditions driven by GNAQ mutations. Among the most prominent of these are vascular malformations, in which aberrant GNAQ signaling contributes to abnormal vascular development and growth. By selectively targeting cells that carry the pathogenic mutation, the therapeutic approach offers the potential for effective intervention while minimizing effects on healthy, non-mutated cells.

The puromycin or puromycin analog may be administered in a range of formulations and by various routes of administration appropriate to the condition being treated. Dosing regimens may be tailored to achieve the desired therapeutic effect, taking into account factors such as the location and extent of the affected tissue, the severity of the condition, and the characteristics of the individual patient.

### Screening Platform

In a further aspect, the invention provides a screening platform for identifying candidate agents capable of modulating diseases associated with GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutations. This platform leverages the observation that mutation-bearing cells exhibit altered responses in cell viability when exposed to effective agents.

According to this screening method, cells harboring a GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutation are contacted with one or more candidate agents. The effect of each candidate agent is then assessed by measuring alterations in cell viability, proliferation, or survival. A candidate agent that reduces the viability or proliferation of mutation-bearing cells is thereby identified as a potential therapeutic agent for the treatment of GNAQ mutation-associated conditions.

This screening approach enables the systematic evaluation of libraries of compounds, facilitating the identification of new agents that act through mechanisms similar to, or distinct from, puromycin. As such, the platform serves as a valuable tool for expanding the repertoire of targeted therapies available for these diseases.

## Advantages and Applications

The invention offers several significant advantages. First, it provides a targeted therapeutic strategy that exploits the specific vulnerability of GNAQ-mutant cells to puromycin and its analogs. Second, it establishes a robust screening methodology for the discovery of additional therapeutic candidates, thereby opening new avenues for research and drug development. Together, these aspects of the invention represent meaningful progress toward more effective and selective treatments for vascular malformations and other conditions driven by GNAQ R183Q and Q209L mutations.

By addressing the underlying molecular basis of these diseases, the present invention holds promise for improving clinical outcomes and expanding the range of therapeutic options available to patients affected by GNAQ mutation-associated disorders.

# GNAQ: The Guanine Nucleotide-Binding Protein G(q) Subunit Alpha

## Overview

**GNAQ** is a gene that encodes the G protein subunit alpha q, a critical member of the guanine nucleotide-binding protein (G protein) family. These proteins act as molecular switches inside cells, transmitting signals from the exterior environment to internal signaling pathways. The GNAQ protein plays an essential role in coupling cell-surface receptors to intracellular responses, influencing numerous physiological processes.

## Molecular Function

The GNAQ protein functions as part of a heterotrimeric G protein complex, consisting of alpha, beta, and gamma subunits. When a signaling molecule binds to a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), the alpha subunit encoded by GNAQ activates downstream effectors, most notably **phospholipase C-beta (PLC-β)**. This activation triggers the production of second messengers such as inositol trisphosphate (IP₃) and diacylglycerol (DAG), which in turn regulate calcium release and protein kinase C activity.

## Clinical Significance

Mutations in the GNAQ gene are associated with several significant medical conditions:

- **Sturge-Weber Syndrome:** A somatic mutation in GNAQ (specifically the R183Q variant) is linked to this neurological disorder, characterized by port-wine birthmarks, glaucoma, and neurological abnormalities.

- **Uveal Melanoma:** GNAQ mutations, particularly at codon 209 (Q209L), are among the most common oncogenic drivers in this eye cancer. These mutations lead to constitutive activation of the protein, promoting uncontrolled cell growth.

- **Congenital Vascular Malformations:** Various nevi and capillary malformations have been connected to mosaic GNAQ mutations.

## Research Importance

Because of its involvement in cancer and developmental disorders, GNAQ remains an active area of biomedical research. Understanding how mutations alter its function offers potential pathways for developing targeted therapies, particularly for uveal melanoma, which currently has limited effective treatment options.

## Conclusion

GNAQ exemplifies how a single gene can influence diverse biological systems. Its role in cellular signaling makes it fundamental to normal development, while its mutations underscore the delicate balance between healthy function and disease. Continued investigation into GNAQ promises to advance both our basic understanding of cell biology and clinical approaches to related conditions.

The present invention relates to compositions and methods for selectively targeting, inhibiting, or eliminating cells harboring activating mutations in the *GNAQ* gene, particularly the R183Q and Q209L mutations. These constitutively activating mutations in the alpha subunit of the heterotrimeric G protein Gq are implicated in a range of pathological conditions, including uveal melanoma, blue nevi, port-wine birthmarks, and Sturge-Weber syndrome. In one aspect, the invention provides methods of using puromycin, or a pharmaceutically acceptable salt, derivative, prodrug, or analog thereof, to target cells bearing a *GNAQ* R183Q or Q209L mutation. In certain embodiments, the invention encompasses methods of treating a disease or disorder associated with a *GNAQ* R183Q or Q209L mutation, comprising administering to a subject in need thereof a therapeutically effective amount of puromycin or a formulation thereof. **Claim 8.** The method of claim 5, wherein puromycin is administered via a route selected from intravenous, intratumoral, topical, intraocular, and local delivery.

**Claim 9.** The method of claim 5, further comprising administering a second therapeutic agent selected from a MEK inhibitor, a PKC inhibitor, a YAP/TAZ pathway inhibitor, and an immune checkpoint inhibitor.

**Claim 10.** The method of claim 5, wherein puromycin is formulated in a targeted delivery vehicle selected from a nanoparticle, liposome, antibody-drug conjugate, and prodrug that preferentially releases active agent in GNAQ-mutant cells.

---

### Screening Application Claims

**Claim 11.** A method of screening for an agent that modulates sensitivity of GNAQ-mutant cells to puromycin, comprising:
- (a) providing a first cell population carrying a GNAQ mutation selected from R183Q, Q209L, or a combination thereof;

- (c) measuring a proliferation or viability parameter of said first cell population; and

**Claim 12.** The method of claim 11, further comprising comparing the response of said first cell population to a second cell population having wild-type GNAQ.

**Claim 13.** A method of identifying a GNAQ-mutant cell in a sample, comprising:
- (a) contacting said sample with puromycin under conditions sufficient to differentially affect proliferation or viability of GNAQ-mutant cells relative to wild-type cells; and

# Invention Statement Aspects: Biotech Patent

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to the fields of molecular biology, vascular pathology, and drug discovery. More specifically, the invention concerns compositions and methods for identifying candidate therapeutic agents useful in the treatment of vascular malformations associated with mutations in the GNAQ gene, employing puromycin-based labeling and selection technologies.

---

## Background Aspects

**Aspect 1 — Disease Context**
Vascular malformations, including capillary malformations (e.g., port-wine birthstains), Sturge-Weber syndrome, and related conditions, are frequently driven by somatic activating mutations in *GNAQ*, most notably the p.R183Q substitution. These mutations constitutively activate downstream Gαq signaling, promoting aberrant endothelial cell proliferation and vessel formation.

**Aspect 2 — Unmet Need**
Current therapeutic options remain limited to laser therapy and surgical intervention, which fail to address the underlying molecular pathology. There exists a significant unmet need for targeted pharmacological agents and for robust screening platforms capable of identifying such agents.

---

## Summary of the Invention (Multiple Claimed Aspects)

### Aspect A — Cell-Based Screening System
A method for identifying a candidate agent for treating a GNAQ-associated vascular malformation, comprising:
- (a) providing a cell population expressing a mutant GNAQ protein (e.g., GNAQ R183Q);
- (b) contacting the cell population with a test agent;
- (c) employing puromycin-based nascent protein labeling (e.g., puromycin, O-propargyl-puromycin, or biotin-puromycin) to quantify translational activity or pathway-specific protein synthesis;
- (d) identifying the test agent as a candidate where it modulates the puromycin-incorporation signal relative to a control.

### Aspect B — Puromycin-Based Selection Construct
A recombinant nucleic acid construct wherein a puromycin resistance marker (*pac* gene) is operably linked to a GNAQ-pathway-responsive regulatory element, such that puromycin survival serves as a reporter of Gαq signaling activity, enabling positive/negative selection during agent screening.

### Aspect C — Ribosome/Translation Profiling Approach
A method utilizing puromycin-associated ribosome profiling (e.g., Puro-seq or SUnSET) to detect alterations in the translatome of GNAQ-mutant endothelial cells upon exposure to candidate agents, thereby identifying agents that normalize mutation-driven protein synthesis dysregulation.

### Aspect D — Candidate Agent Identification Workflow
A high-throughput workflow comprising isogenic paired cell lines differing only in GNAQ mutation status, wherein differential puromycin-labeling readouts between mutant and wild-type cells define a therapeutic window and enable selective agent identification.

---

## Detailed Enablement Aspects

**Aspect 1 — Cellular Models**
Suitable cells include human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), induced pluripotent stem cell-derived endothelial cells, or immortalized endothelial lines engineered (e.g., via CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in) to harbor GNAQ R183Q, R183G, Q209L, or Q209P mutations.

**Aspect 2 — Puromycin Detection Modalities**
Detection may employ anti-puromycin antibodies, click-chemistry conjugation to fluorophores (for OPP), affinity capture of biotin-puromycin-labeled peptides, or growth/survival assays under puromycin selection.

**Aspect 3 — Candidate Agent Classes**
Test agents may include small molecules, kinase inhibitors, Gαq-selective inhibitors (e.g., FR900359/YM-254890 analogs), MEK/ERK pathway inhibitors, siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, or antibody fragments.

**Aspect 4 — Readout Metrics**
Modulation may be assessed as reduction in aberrant nascent protein synthesis, restoration of normal proliferation, decreased downstream effector phosphorylation, or altered puromycin-resistance survival kinetics.

---

## Representative Claim Language (Illustrative)

> **Claim 1.** A method of identifying a candidate agent for the treatment of a vascular malformation, the method comprising: contacting a cell harboring an activating GNAQ mutation with a test agent; performing puromycin incorporation labeling to measure nascent polypeptide synthesis; and identifying the test agent as a candidate agent when it reduces puromycin incorporation relative to an untreated control cell harboring said GNAQ mutation.

> **Claim 2.** The method of Claim 1, wherein the GNAQ mutation is selected from R183Q, R183G, Q209L, and Q209P.

> **Claim 3.** The method of Claim 1, wherein the puromycin labeling comprises use of O-propargyl-puromycin followed by copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition detection.

---

*Note: This content is provided as a drafting aid to illustrate patent-document structure and terminology. It should be reviewed, validated against prior art (freedom-to-operate and novelty searches), and finalized by a licensed patent attorney or agent before any filing.*
